# simoom

> simoom is an embeddable HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 server engine for Rust, with TLS 1.3, WebSocket and an HTTP client. It uses only the Rust standard library: no tokio, no hyper, no rustls and no OpenSSL. It runs one event loop per core on epoll or io_uring (Linux), IOCP (Windows) or kqueue (macOS), and is built for edge devices, serverless functions and servers. It is the HTTP engine behind Cameleer (https://github.com/Cameleering/cameleer), and it is a Cameleering project (https://cameleer.ing/cameleering/). Licence: Apache-2.0. Status: version 0.1.0, before the first release, not on crates.io yet.

## Facts

- Repository: https://github.com/Cameleering/simoom
- Add it: `cargo add simoom`, or `simoom = "0.1"` in `Cargo.toml` (Rust 1.89+; https://crates.io/crates/simoom, docs at https://docs.rs/simoom). For HTTP/1.1 only: `default-features = false, features = ["http1"]`. The client: `cargo add simoom-client`.
- API: `Server::builder().listen(addr).service(f).start()`. A service is `Fn(&mut Request, Reply) -> Outcome` and runs on the loop thread. `Router` handles paths and methods. Blocking work goes through `simoom::blocking` (a bounded offload pool) or `Reply::defer` (answer from your own thread through a `Responder`). `Reply::stream` and `Reply::sse` stream bodies, and `Reply::websocket` upgrades to a WebSocket. No async runtime is needed.
- TLS: `simoom::tls::{CertifiedKey, ServerConfig}` with `Builder::listen_tls` and `.tls(cfg)`. HTTP/3: `Builder::listen_quic` and `.quic_tls(cfg)` (features `tls` and `http3`, or `full`).
- Client: the `simoom-client` crate provides `Client::builder()...build()`, `client.get(url).send()` and `HttpVersion::{Auto, Http1, Http2, Http3}`.
- Cargo features: `http1`, `http2`, `websocket` and `io-uring` (default); `tls`, `tls-extra`, `http3`, `full`; `compression`, `brotli`, `zstd`; `websocket-h2`, `websocket-h3`, `ws-deflate`, `h2-keepalive`; `multipart`, `cookies`, `conditional`, `cors`, `auth`.
- Not included: a static-file server, a reverse proxy, a configuration-file web server, QUIC 0-RTT (refused by design) and ECN.

## Measured

Same DigitalOcean c-4 droplet, open-loop load from two separate nodes, SLO = p99 ≤ 1 ms:

- Plaintext GET with a 13-byte reply, 256 connections (2026-11-12): 172,638 req/s, against 144,443 for hyper and 150,673 for may-minihttp. At 64 connections: 170,648, 122,240 and 158,598.
- TLS 1.3 handshakes (2026-11-11): 10,083 full and 11,213 resumed per second, against 7,711 and 7,758 for h2o. The same plaintext test over TLS: 160,441 req/s, against 97,219 for h2o.
- HTTP/3: 106,947 req/s, against 94,507 for h2o. CPU per request at 50k req/s: 25.05 µs, against 28.10 µs for hyper.
- Memory per idle connection with 100k open: 520-533 B, against 532 B for nginx.
- Cold start to first response: 0.73 ms plain and 0.87 ms with TLS, against 0.77 ms and 1.37 ms for Cameleer's previous HTTP server on the same machine. Idle PSS is about 1 MB.
- Code a build adds to a binary (stripped, x86-64 Linux): 214,568 B for HTTP/1.1 only (budget 250 KB) and 935,064 B for the full server with HTTP/3 (budget 1 MB).

Where simoom is behind:

- Under overload at 1.17x the NIC ceiling, nginx answers more requests within 1 ms (52.4k against 6.4k), although simoom has the higher total goodput (160.3k against 145.5k).
- may-minihttp holds up better on a degraded network path.
- haproxy's p99 under slowloris attack is 8% lower.

## Verification

- h2spec 2.6.0: 146/146.
- QUIC Interop Runner against ngtcp2, quiche and quic-go: 54 of 58 supported pairs (the failures are 0-RTT, refused by design, and ECN, not implemented).
- HTTP Garden: 0 desyncs.
- testssl.sh: no vulnerabilities found.
- Hermetic test suite: 777 tests on Windows and 791 on Linux.
- No independent audit yet.
